outcome: Salivary cortisol level (at rest and post-stressor)
Behavioural response to physical stressors (crying vigor)
cohort: The study included 65 Term-Low Birth Weight (T-LBW) neonates as cases and 67 Term-Normal Birth Weight (T-NBW) neonates as controls, matched for age (4-6 hours), gestational age, and mode of delivery.
finding: The severity of intrauterine growth retardation correlated with behavioral and physiological inhibition, characterized by poorer anthropometry, lower basal and inhibited post-stress cortisol responses, and less vigorous crying in affected term neonates.
birth_weight: Term-Low Birth Weight (cases) and Term-Normal Birth Weight (controls)
